questions.stem: $Spany$ sells seeds and claims that 5% of its pansy seeds do not germinate. A packet of pansy seeds contains 20 seeds. Each seed germinates independently of the other seeds.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the probability that in a packet of $Spany$'s pansy seeds
(i) more than 2 but fewer than 5 seeds do not germinate,
(ii) more than 18 seeds germinate.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) B1: writing or using $X \sim \mathrm{B}(20,0.05)$ or $Y \sim \mathrm{B}(20,0.95)$ [Allow $Y \sim \mathrm{B}(20,0.95)$ if $Y$ is clearly defined]. Implied by 1 correct prob.
(i) M1: for $\mathrm{P}(X \leqslant 4)-\mathrm{P}(X \leqslant 2)$ and one correct prob, or $\mathrm{P}(X=3)+\mathrm{P}(X=4)$ and 1 correct prob: $\mathrm{P}(X \leqslant 4)-\mathrm{P}(X \leqslant 2) = 0.9974-0.9245$ or $\binom{20}{3}0.05^3\times0.95^{17}+\binom{20}{4}0.05^4\times0.95^{16}=0.05958\ldots+0.01332\ldots$
A1: $= 0.072909\ldots$ awrt $0.0729$
(ii) M1: for $\mathrm{P}(X \leqslant 1)$ or $[20]\times(0.95)^{19}(0.05)+(0.95)^{20}$ - condone missing 20: $\mathrm{P}(X \leqslant 1)$ or $\mathrm{P}(Y \geqslant 19)=20\times(0.95)^{19}(0.05)+(0.95)^{20}$
A1: $= 0.7358$ or $= 0.735839\ldots$ awrt $0.736$

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Jem buys 5 packets of $Spany$'s pansy seeds.
(b) Calculate the probability that all of these packets contain more than 18 seeds that germinate.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) [Let $W$ = no. of packets where $Y > 18$] M1: $\mathrm{P}(W=5)=(\text{"}0.7358\ldots\text{"})^5$ for (their(a)(ii))$^5$
A1: $= 0.21573\ldots$ awrt $0.216$

parts.label: c
parts.text:
Jem believes that $Spany$'s claim is incorrect. She believes that the percentage of pansy seeds that do not germinate is greater than 5%
(c) Write down the hypotheses for a suitable test to examine Jem's belief.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme: (c) B1: $\mathrm{H_0}: p=0.05$, $\mathrm{H_1}: p>0.05$ - both hypotheses correct with $p$ or $\pi$

parts.label: d
parts.text:
Jem planted all of the 100 seeds she bought from $Spany$ and found that 8 did not germinate.
(d) Using a suitable approximation, carry out the test using a 5% level of significance.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) [$V$= no. of seeds that do not germinate $V \sim \mathrm{B}(100,0.05)$ approximates to $V \sim \mathrm{Po}(5)$] M1A1 (1st M1: for realising a Poisson approximation is appropriate. NB Po(95) is M0A0; 1st A1: writing or using $V \sim \mathrm{Po}(5)$ i.e. correct mean for the Poisson.)
$\mathrm{P}(V \geqslant 8) = 1-\mathrm{P}(V \leqslant 7) = 1-0.8666 = 0.1334$ (2nd M1: for writing or using $1-\mathrm{P}(V \leqslant 7)$ or $\mathrm{P}(V \leqslant 7)=0.8666$ or writing $\mathrm{P}(V \geqslant 10)=0.0318$ or $\mathrm{P}(V \geqslant 9)=0.0681$ or $\mathrm{P}(V \geqslant 11)=0.0137$ leading to a CR. Implied by correct CR or probability = awrt 0.133)
CR for 1-tail in (c): $\mathrm{P}(V \geqslant 9)=0.0681$, $\mathrm{P}(V \geqslant 10)=0.0318$, CR $V \geqslant 10$ oe
CR for 2-tail in (c): $\mathrm{P}(V \geqslant 10)=0.0318$, $\mathrm{P}(V \geqslant 11)=0.0137$, CR $V \geqslant 11$ oe
(2nd A1: for awrt 0.133 or $V \geqslant 10$ oe (e.g. $V>9$) or $V \geqslant 11$ oe allow any letter but CR must match part(c))
dM1: dep on 2nd M1. Accept H0 or not significant or 8 does not lie in the critical region ft their CR or probability. A correct statement based on comparing 8 with their CR or their prob with 0.05 or 0.025 [condone 0.866<0.95]- contradicting non-contextual comments M0
A1cso: (dep, all previous marks must be awarded, need Bold words) Data consistent with $Spany$'s claim or Insufficient evidence for Jem's belief or insufficient evidence that percentage of seeds not germinating is more than 5% (o.e.)
NB award M1A1 for a correct contextual statement on its own. If there are no hypotheses or they are the wrong way around, then 3rd M0 3rd A0.
SC1 Normal approximation: Award marks in pairs with 2, 4 or 6 marks available. Sight of $\mathrm{N}(5\text{ or }95, \sqrt{4.75}^2)$ M1A1; probability awrt 0.125/6 M1A1; Correct contextual concl' dM1A1
SC2 No approximation: Use of $\mathrm{B}(100,0.05)$ M0A0; probability awrt 0.128 or CR $\geqslant 10$ M1A1; then M0A0

questions.stem:
The random variable $Y \sim \mathrm{B}(225, p)$

Using a normal approximation, the probability that $Y$ is at least 188 is 0.1056 to 4 decimal places.

parts.text:
(i) Show that $p$ satisfies $145p^2-241p+100=0$ when the normal probability tables are used.
(ii) Hence find the value of $p$, justifying your answer.
(10)
parts.mark_scheme:
(i) B1: $z=1.25$ or better (calculator gives: 1.25027…)
M1: for attempting to use a continuity correction i.e. for sight of $188 \pm 0.5$
M1: for standardising using $\mu$ and $\sigma$ or $np$ and $\sqrt{np(1-p)}$ (Condone letter $n$ or any integer $>0$)
A1: for a correct equation with compatible signs, allow 1.250…, $\frac{187.5-\mu}{\sigma}=1.25$ leading to $187.5-\mu=1.25\sigma$
M1: for $\mu=225p$ seen at any stage in the working
M1: for $\sigma=\sqrt{225p(1-p)}$ seen at any stage in the working. Must be for $\sigma$ not $\sigma^2=225p(1-p)$
M1: for squaring to get a quadratic equation in $p$: $(187.5-225p)^2=(1.25)^2\times225p(1-p)$ or $(150-180p)^2=225p(1-p)$ (o.e.)
A1*: (dep on all previous Ms and use of 1.25 (with correct sign) for at least 1 correct intermediate step from a correct quadratic equation e.g. one of those in scheme for 5th M1): e.g. $900(5-6p)^2=225(p-p^2) \Rightarrow 4(25-60p+36p^2)=p-p^2$ leading to $145p^2-241p+100=0$*
(ii) M1: for solving the quadratic correctly - leading to $p=\ldots$ or implied by 0.8 or awrt 0.862: $[(29p-25)(5p-4)=0 \Rightarrow]$ $p=0.8$ or $p=\frac{25}{29}$ (accept 0.862(0689…))
A1: for 0.8 and a correct reason to eliminate 0.862: $[p=]$ $0.8$ because 0.862 gives a mean greater than 188 (oe)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- 1st A1: If using a value for $n$ it must be 225

questions.notes: Question 6 is a single printed mark bracket (10) covering both (i) and (ii), so treated as one part with label null.
